name: New Delhi
intro: Mughal tombs and forts, the bustling lanes of Old Delhi, British-era boulevards and peaceful gardens. Distances are big: the metro is fast, cheap and air-conditioned, with app taxis for the gaps.

transit.card: Delhi Metro QR ticket (app or counter) or a travel card
transit.note: Metro runs roughly 5:30–23:30; every station has a security check.

sources: Written from general knowledge for the MVP; needs a human review before launch

areas.name: Old Delhi
areas.blurb: Red Fort, Jama Masjid and the lanes of Chandni Chowk.

areas.name: Connaught Place
areas.blurb: Colonnaded circle of shops, a stepwell and a gurudwara.

areas.name: India Gate & Kartavya Path
areas.blurb: War memorials, museums and the Old Fort.

areas.name: Humayun's Tomb & Nizamuddin
areas.blurb: The tomb that inspired the Taj, and a Sufi shrine.

areas.name: Lodhi Garden & Khan Market
areas.blurb: Tomb-dotted garden and a smart market.

areas.name: Hauz Khas
areas.blurb: Medieval ruins around a lake, with cafés.

areas.name: Qutub Minar & Mehrauli
areas.blurb: The 73 m minaret and an archaeological park.

areas.name: Lotus Temple
areas.blurb: The flower-shaped house of worship in the south.

areas.name: Akshardham
areas.blurb: The vast carved temple complex in the east.

areas.name: Chanakyapuri
areas.blurb: The embassy district with the Rail Museum.

pois.name: Red Fort
pois.why: The Mughal emperors' red sandstone fort, where the Prime Minister speaks on Independence Day.
pois.kid: Find the Hall of Public Audience where the emperor sat on a marble throne.
pois.tip: Buy tickets online for a lower price and a quicker entry.

pois.name: Jama Masjid
pois.why: India's largest mosque, built by Shah Jahan, with a courtyard for 25,000 people.
pois.kid: Climb the minaret (small fee) for a view over Old Delhi.
pois.tip: Closed to visitors at prayer times. Shoulders and legs covered; robes are lent at the gate.

pois.name: Chandni Chowk
pois.why: Old Delhi's great market street; take a cycle rickshaw through the side lanes.
pois.kid: A cycle-rickshaw ride is the fun way to see it.
pois.tip: Many shops close on Sundays. Agree the rickshaw fare first.

pois.name: Gurudwara Sis Ganj Sahib
pois.why: A Sikh temple on Chandni Chowk marking the place where the ninth Guru was martyred.
pois.tip: Cover your head and remove shoes; scarves are provided.

pois.name: Paranthe Wali Gali
pois.why: A narrow lane of family shops frying stuffed parathas since the 1870s.
pois.tip: Ask for less chilli for kids.

pois.name: Karim's
pois.why: A legendary Mughlai restaurant by Jama Masjid, cooking kebabs and curries since 1913.

pois.name: Gurudwara Bangla Sahib
pois.why: A white-and-gold Sikh temple with a sacred pool and a free kitchen that feeds thousands every day.
pois.kid: Peek into the kitchen where volunteers make rotis by the thousand.
pois.tip: Cover your head, remove shoes and wash your feet at the entrance; scarves are provided.

pois.name: Agrasen ki Baoli
pois.why: A deep medieval stepwell with over 100 stone steps, hidden among office blocks.
pois.kid: Count the steps on the way down.

pois.name: Jantar Mantar
pois.why: An 18th-century observatory of giant stone instruments, including a huge sundial.
pois.kid: Tell the time by the shadow on the giant sundial.

pois.name: Janpath market
pois.why: Street stalls of textiles, jewellery and souvenirs.

pois.name: India Gate
pois.why: The 42 m war memorial arch at the end of Kartavya Path, lit up in the evening.
pois.kid: Find names of soldiers carved into the arch.
pois.tip: Lively in the evening with families and ice-cream sellers.

pois.name: National War Memorial
pois.why: Circular memorial to soldiers who died for independent India.

pois.name: National Museum
pois.why: India's big history museum: Harappan seals, sculptures and royal treasures.
pois.kid: Find the 4,500-year-old 'Dancing Girl' bronze from the Indus Valley.

pois.name: Kartavya Path & Rashtrapati Bhavan view
pois.why: The ceremonial avenue up Raisina Hill to the President's House.

pois.name: Purana Qila (Old Fort)
pois.why: A 16th-century fort with huge gates and a boating lake below the walls.
pois.kid: Row a pedal boat around the fort moat.

pois.name: National Crafts Museum
pois.why: Village houses, textiles and craftspeople at work.
pois.kid: Watch an artisan at work in the courtyard.

pois.name: Humayun's Tomb
pois.why: A 16th-century Mughal garden tomb, the model for the Taj Mahal.
pois.kid: Walk the four-part garden and find the water channels.
pois.tip: Early morning light is beautiful and it's cooler.

pois.name: Sunder Nursery
pois.why: A restored Mughal garden park with lawns, ponds and tombs.

pois.name: Nizamuddin Dargah
pois.why: A 14th-century Sufi shrine reached through busy lanes; qawwali music on Thursday evenings.
pois.tip: Cover your head; women cannot enter the inner tomb chamber.

pois.name: Lodhi Garden
pois.why: A large garden with 15th-century tombs among the lawns.
pois.kid: Spot the parakeets in the trees.

pois.name: Dilli Haat INA
pois.why: An open-air craft bazaar with food stalls from every Indian state.
pois.kid: Try a dish from a state you've never heard of.

pois.name: National Rail Museum
pois.why: Steam engines, royal saloons and a toy train ride around the grounds.
pois.kid: Ride the little toy train around the museum.

pois.name: Nehru Park
pois.why: A big green park in the embassy district.

pois.name: Qutub Minar
pois.why: A 73 m 12th-century minaret of red sandstone, plus an iron pillar that doesn't rust.
pois.kid: The iron pillar is over 1,600 years old and still hasn't rusted.

pois.name: Mehrauli Archaeological Park
pois.why: Woodland dotted with tombs, stepwells and mosques.
pois.tip: Go in daylight and in a group.

pois.name: Hauz Khas fort & lake
pois.why: Medieval college ruins overlooking a lake, popular at sunset.

pois.name: Deer Park
pois.why: A park next to Hauz Khas with deer, rabbits and ducks.

pois.name: Lotus Temple
pois.why: A Bahá'í house of worship shaped like a white lotus flower, open to all.
pois.tip: Silence inside; shoes off at the entrance.

pois.name: Akshardham
pois.costNote: Temple free; exhibitions and water show paid
pois.why: A huge carved pink-and-white temple complex with exhibitions and an evening water show.
pois.kid: Count the stone elephants around the base of the temple.
pois.tip: No phones or bags allowed inside: leave them at the cloakroom.

pois.name: Connaught Place cafés
pois.why: Restaurants and cafés around the white colonnades of the inner circle.

pois.name: Pandara Road restaurants
pois.why: A short row of classic North Indian restaurants near India Gate.

pois.name: Khan Market
pois.why: A compact market of cafés, bakeries and bookshops near Lodhi Garden.

pois.name: Hauz Khas Village cafés
pois.why: Cafés with views over the lake and ruins.

pois.name: Nizamuddin kebab stalls
pois.why: Kebabs and breads from small shops in the lanes near the dargah.

pois.name: Akshardham food court
pois.why: Vegetarian food court inside the complex.

dayTrips.name: Agra (Taj Mahal)
dayTrips.from: Gatimaan Express or Vande Bharat from Hazrat Nizamuddin or New Delhi to Agra Cantt
dayTrips.why: The Taj Mahal at sunrise, plus Agra Fort, on a long day by fast train.
highlights: Mehtab Bagh sunset view across the river
dayTrips.tip: The Taj is closed on Fridays. Book trains well ahead and buy Taj tickets online.

dayTrips.name: Mathura & Vrindavan
dayTrips.from: Train from Hazrat Nizamuddin or New Delhi to Mathura Junction
dayTrips.why: Krishna's birthplace and the temple town of Vrindavan nearby.
dayTrips.tip: Temples close in the early afternoon; go early.

dayTrips.name: Chandigarh
dayTrips.why: Le Corbusier's planned city with the whimsical Rock Garden.
dayTrips.tip: A very long day; only worth it with an early train.

tips.title: Getting around
tips.text: Use the metro for long hops: buy QR tickets in the DMRC app or at the counter. The first coach is for women only. App taxis (Uber, Ola) and auto-rickshaws fill the gaps; agree or check the fare first.

tips.title: Season
tips.text: October to March is the best time. April to June is very hot (40 °C+), July to September is monsoon. In winter, check the air quality and fog before planning outdoor days.

tips.title: Dress and manners
tips.text: Cover shoulders and legs at temples, mosques and gurudwaras. Remove shoes; cover your head at gurudwaras and mosques (scarves are usually provided).

tips.title: Food and water
tips.text: Drink only bottled or filtered water. Eat at busy places where food is cooked fresh. Many Indian dishes can be made 'less spicy' on request.

tips.title: Monuments
tips.text: Many museums and Akshardham close on Mondays. Buy monument tickets online (ASI) for lower prices and shorter queues.

tips.title: Safety
tips.text: Watch for touts at stations offering 'help' with tickets. Emergency number: 112.
